svg.title: From One Account to a $10,000 Monthly Residual Book
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-residual-book-funnel; chapter number: 6; title: From One Account to a $10,000 Monthly Residual Book; subtitle: Merchant-count milestones reported by working agents; chart type: funnel; stages: label: Target book with safety buffer; value: 50; display: 50 merchants for about $10,000 per month; conversion: 35 core clients plus a 15-client buffer; detail: Residual Builders adds 15 to 20 clients on top of the raw count to absorb shortfalls and cancels.; label: Core clients at $400 each; value: 35; display: 35 clients; conversion: Raw count before the buffer; detail: Residual Builders models $300 to $400 per client when planning a $10,000 monthly target.; label: Twenty-sale milestone; value: 20; display: About $600 in new monthly residual; conversion: About $30 per account per month; detail: James Shepard's average across agents selling for North American Bank Card and Total Merchant Services.; label: Ten-sale milestone; value: 10; display: About $300 in new monthly residual; conversion: About $30 per account per month; detail: Shepard benchmarks an industry-average split of about 50% and about $275 average upfront.; label: First active account; value: 1; display: About $30 per month; conversion: Paid roughly two months behind the sale; detail: Electronic Money Company recalls a first residual check of $187; Ryan Anthony pegs accounts at $100 to $500 a month.; caption: Residual income compounds one account at a time, and practitioners plan for cancels by over-building the merchant count.; assumptions note: Per-account figures differ by practitioner, from about $30 (Shepard) to $300-$400 (Residual Builders); milestones are not one agent's book.; note: Sources include Residual Builders, James Shepard of CCSalesPro, Ryan Anthony, and Electronic Money Company.

text.title: From One Account to a $10,000 Monthly Residual Book
text.tspan: From One Account to a $10,000 Monthly Residual Book

rect.title: label: Target book with safety buffer; value: 50; display: 50 merchants for about $10,000 per month; conversion: 35 core clients plus a 15-client buffer; detail: Residual Builders adds 15 to 20 clients on top of the raw count to absorb shortfalls and cancels.

label: Core clients at $400 each; value: 35; display: 35 clients; conversion: Raw count before the buffer; detail: Residual Builders models $300 to $400 per client when planning a $10,000 monthly target.

label: Twenty-sale milestone; value: 20; display: About $600 in new monthly residual; conversion: About $30 per account per month; detail: James Shepard's average across agents selling for North American Bank Card and Total Merchant Services.

label: Ten-sale milestone; value: 10; display: About $300 in new monthly residual; conversion: About $30 per account per month; detail: Shepard benchmarks an industry-average split of about 50% and about $275 average upfront.

label: First active account; value: 1; display: About $30 per month; conversion: Paid roughly two months behind the sale; detail: Electronic Money Company recalls a first residual check of $187; Ryan Anthony pegs accounts at $100 to $500 a month.

text.title: Assumptions: Per-account figures differ by practitioner, from about $30 (Shepard) to $300-$400 (Residual Builders); milestones are not one agent's book.
